description: Sahyadri Bank, a private sector bank regulated by the RBI, wants new savings account customers to complete KYC entirely through its mobile app using video-based customer identification. Today customers visit a branch with their Aadhaar and PAN cards, and staff upload the records to the Central KYC Records Registry the next day. In the new flow the customer gives consent, completes Aadhaar OTP-based e-KYC, uploads their PAN, and joins a live video call with a trained bank official who matches their face against the Aadhaar photo and asks a few questions. Calls from IP addresses outside India must be blocked, and the video recordings and all customer data must be stored on servers in India. Accounts must not become operational until the video check and a review of the recording are complete. The app will hold Aadhaar numbers, PAN, photographs and video recordings, so the security team insists on encryption, access logs and a quick response to any breach. The bank's internal audit team will review the onboarding controls, and the RBI may inspect them. The account opening journey is new to the digital team, and the video-KYC vendor platform has not been integrated with the core banking system before. The bank expects about 5,000 applications a day and wants to launch before Diwali.

clauses.text: (1) The bank shall develop an application for digital KYC process and make it available at customer touch points for undertaking KYC of its customers and shall undertake the KYC process only through this authenticated application. (2) The bank shall control the access to the Application and shall ensure that unauthorised persons do not use it. Authorised officials shall access the Application only through a login-id and password or a Live OTP or Time OTP controlled mechanism that the bank provides. (3) The customer, for the purpose of KYC, shall visit the location of the authorised official of the bank or vice-versa. The original OVD shall be in possession of the customer. (4) The bank shall ensure that the authorised officer takes a Live photograph of the customer and embeds the same photograph in the Customer Application Form (CAF). Further, the bank’s system Application shall put a watermark in readable form, containing the CAF number, GPS coordinates, authorised official’s name, unique employee code (which the bank assigns) and date (DD:MM:YYYY) and time stamp (HH:MM:SS), on the captured live photograph of the customer.

requirement_questions.question: What is the definition of 'complete KYC entirely through the mobile app' in terms of customer journey and data handling?
options: The customer completes all identity verification, document uploads, and video verification via the app without any branch visit or physical interaction.
The customer uploads documents and initiates e-KYC via the app, but must visit a branch for final verification and account activation.
The customer completes document uploads via the app, but the video call is conducted in person at a branch with a bank officer.
The mobile app only serves as a portal to initiate the process, with the actual KYC completed at a branch with staff assistance.

requirement_questions.question: How should money laundering and terrorist financing risks be assessed for new customers during the video-KYC process?
options: Automated risk scoring based on PAN, Aadhaar, and transaction patterns with real-time risk alerts to auditors.
Manual review by a compliance officer for every customer, with no automated tools or thresholds.
Risk assessment based solely on the customer's address and PAN, with no additional data or behavioral analysis.
Risk assessment is performed only for high-risk customers identified by a predefined list, with no automated screening.

requirement_questions.question: How will the system determine if a customer is a politically exposed person (PEP), and what action will be taken if confirmed?
options: The system checks against a real-time PEP database maintained by the RBI and applies enhanced due diligence automatically.
The system flags PEP status for manual review by a compliance officer, with no automated screening or database.
PEP status is not checked, and the system assumes all customers are non-PEPs by default.
PEP status is verified only if the customer provides a self-declared statement, with no automated checks.

requirement_questions.question: Who is responsible for conducting the concurrent audit of the video KYC process and recording before account activation?
options: A designated internal auditor from the bank's internal audit team performs the audit independently.
The RBI conducts the audit as part of its regulatory inspection process.
The video-KYC vendor platform performs the audit and provides a report to the bank.
The system automatically triggers a review by a bank officer without requiring a separate audit step.

srs.title: Sahyadri Bank Mobile App for Video-Based KYC
srs.purpose: To enable new savings account customers to complete their Know Your Customer (KYC) process entirely through the mobile app using video-based authentication, ensuring compliance with RBI regulations and enhancing digital accessibility.
srs.scope: The system supports end-to-end digital KYC for new savings account applicants via mobile app, including Aadhaar OTP-based e-KYC, live video verification with bank officials, face matching, and PAN upload. It does not include account management, loan processing, or post-activation services. The system is limited to customers within India and does not support cross-border video calls or offline verification without integration with the core banking system.

stakeholders.interest: Convenient, secure, and transparent account opening process with clear data usage and consent mechanisms
Ability to review onboarding controls and KYC processes for compliance and risk assessment
Inspection and audit of KYC processes and compliance with regulatory requirements
Protection of customer data, prevention of spoofing, and rapid response to security incidents

srs.operating_environment: The system operates on Android and iOS mobile devices with internet connectivity. It functions within India only, with video calls blocked from external IP addresses. The application must support up to 5,000 daily account applications and maintain 99.9% uptime during peak hours leading up to Diwali.
constraints: Video calls must originate only from IP addresses within India [P4].
All customer data, including Aadhaar, PAN, photos, and recordings, must be stored on servers located in India [NFR-SEC-02].
The system must not activate any new savings account until the video KYC process and recording review are completed [FR-08].
The system must implement end-to-end encryption and maintain access logs for all data interactions [NFR-SEC-03, NFR-SEC-04].
The system must prevent spoofing through face liveness detection [NFR-SEC-06].
assumptions: The video-KYC vendor platform is integrated with the mobile app and core banking system as per the requirements.
Customers provide explicit consent for data collection and use, and are aware of the data being collected and its purpose.
The core banking system is capable of receiving KYC verification results and activating accounts only after audit completion.

regulations.name: RBI IT Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Directions 2023 (India; marked withdrawn)

obligations.text: Follow a formally defined project management approach with stakeholder participation, and put new applications through product approval and quality assurance.
obligations.excerpt: 12. Project Management (a) REs shall follow a consistent and formally defined project management approach for IT projects undertaken by them. The project management approach shall, inter alia, enable appropriate stakeholder participation for effective monitoring and management of project risks and progress. (b) While adopting new or emerging technologies, tools, or revamping their existing ones in the technology stack, REs shall follow a standard enterprise architecture planning methodology or framework. (c) Adoption of new or emerging technologies shall be commensurate with the risk appetite and align with overall Business/ IT strategy of the RE. It should facilitate optimal creation, use, or sharing of information by a business in a secure and resilient way. (d) REs shall maintain enterprise data dictionary to enable the sharing of data among applications and information systems and promote a common understanding of data. (e) REs shall ensure that maintenance and necessary support of software applications is provided by the software vendors and the same is enforced through formal agreement.

obligations.text: Obtain the vendor's written confirmation that the application is free of known vulnerabilities and malware, again after every material change.
obligations.excerpt: (f) REs shall obtain the source codes for all critical applications from their vendors. Where obtaining of the source code is not possible, REs shall put in place a source code escrow arrangement or other arrangements to adequately mitigate the risk of default by the vendor. REs shall ensure that all product updates and programme fixes are included in the source code escrow arrangement. (g) REs shall obtain a certificate or a written confirmation from the application developer or vendor stating that the application is free of known vulnerabilities, malware, and any covert channels in the code. Such a certificate or a written confirmation shall also be obtained whenever material changes to the code, including upgrades, occur. (h) Any new IT application proposed to be introduced as a business product13 shall be subjected to product approval and quality assurance process.

obligations.text: Assess, approve, document and review every change and patch, with a way to recover from failed changes.
obligations.excerpt: 13. Change and Patch Management REs shall put in place documented policy(ies) and procedures for change and patch management to ensure the following: (a) the business impact of implementing patches/ changes (or not implementing a particular patch/ change request) are assessed; (b) the patches/ changes are applied/ implemented and reviewed in a secure and timely manner with necessary approvals; (c) any changes to an application system or data are justified by genuine business needs and approvals supported by documentation and subjected to a robust change management process; and (d) mechanism is established to recover from failed changes/ patch deployment or unexpected results. 14. Data Migration Controls REs shall have a documented data migration policy specifying a systematic process for data migration, ensuring data integrity, completeness and consistency. The policy shall, inter alia, contain provisions pertaining to signoffs from business users and application owners at each stage of migration, maintenance of audit trails, etc. 13 IT Applications that enable functioning of a business process whether offered as a product to the customers (including potential customers), third parties (or) internal employees could be broadly referred as business product.

obligations.text: Keep audit trails detailed enough for audit and forensics, and monitor them regularly.
obligations.excerpt: 15. Audit Trails (a) Every IT application which can access or affect critical or sensitive information, shall have necessary audit and system logging capability and should provide audit trails. (b) The audit trails shall satisfy a RE’s business requirements apart from regulatory and legal requirements. The audit trails must be detailed enough to facilitate the conduct of audit, serve as forensic evidence when required and assist in dispute resolution, including for non-repudiation purposes. (c) REs shall put in place a system for regularly monitoring the audit trails and system logs to detect any unauthorised activity. 16. Cryptographic controls The key length, algorithms, cipher suites and applicable protocols used in transmission channels, processing of data and authentication purpose shall be strong. REs shall adopt internationally accepted and published standards that are not deprecated/ demonstrated to be insecure/ vulnerable and the configurations involved in implementing such controls shall be compliant with extant laws and regulatory instructions.

obligations.text: Define RTO and RPO, run DR drills at least half-yearly for critical systems, and test backup restores.
obligations.excerpt: (d) REs shall regularly test the BCP / DR under different scenarios for possible types of contingencies, to ensure that it is up-to-date and effective. (e) REs shall backup data and periodically restore such backed-up data to check its usability. The integrity of such backup data shall be preserved along with securing it from unauthorised access. (f) REs shall ensure that DR architecture and procedures are robust, meeting the defined RTO and RPO for any recovery operations in case of contingency. (g) REs should prioritise achieving minimal RTO (as approved by the RE’s ITSC) and a near zero RPO for critical information systems. (h) In a scenario of non-zero RPO, REs shall have a documented methodology for reconciliation of data while resuming operations from the alternate location. questions.question:
How often are requirements expected to change during and after development?
   low = Changes are rare (e.g., yearly or only through formal change control).
   medium = Occasional planned change (e.g., quarterly adjustments).
   high = Features are expected to change continuously based on feedback or competition.

How frequently must working software reach production?
   low = One or very few releases (about yearly or rarer); deployment is costly or physically constrained.
   medium = Every two weeks to quarterly, inclusive - fortnightly, monthly and quarterly all count as medium.
   high = Weekly or more often, or on demand.

What happens if the software fails?
   low = Minor inconvenience.
   medium = Noticeable business disruption or recoverable financial loss.
   high = Safety harm, large financial loss, or serious legal/reputational damage.

How much does the project depend on existing legacy systems?
   low = Greenfield with no legacy constraints.
   medium = Some integration with existing systems.
   high = Must integrate with, replace, or migrate data from legacy systems.

The audit trails must be detailed enough to facilitate the conduct of audit, serve as forensic evidence when required and assist in dispute resolution, including for non-repudiation purposes.
